# `system` — `/api/system`

System router — health of the services the app uses, GPU information and the GPU job queue, CPU mode, and restarting the backend (source checkouts only).

| Method | Path | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| GET | [`/api/system/cpu-mode`](#get-api-system-cpu-mode) | {enabled, setting: auto\|on\|off, nvidia_gpu}. |
| PUT | [`/api/system/cpu-mode`](#put-api-system-cpu-mode) | The owner's choice from Tools: auto (on without an NVIDIA GPU), on or off. |
| GET | [`/api/system/gpu`](#get-api-system-gpu) | Return raw GPU stats from nvidia-smi. |
| GET | [`/api/system/gpu-queue`](#get-api-system-gpu-queue) | Read-only view of the single-GPU serialization queue. |
| GET | [`/api/system/hardware`](#get-api-system-hardware) | Returns hardware profile with capability hints for the UI. |
| POST | [`/api/system/restart`](#post-api-system-restart) | Restart the backend worker by touching backend/api.py. |
| GET | [`/api/system/status`](#get-api-system-status) | Parallel health check for Ollama, TTS, SD, Prometheus, and GPU. |

<a id="get-api-system-cpu-mode"></a>
### `GET /api/system/cpu-mode`

{enabled, setting: auto|on|off, nvidia_gpu}. See backend/services/machine.py.

- Handler: [`get_cpu_mode`](../../../backend/routers/system.py)
- Access: this computer only, or the API key once `ARYNWOOD_API_KEY` is set

**Response**

- `200`: JSON object with `enabled`, `setting`, `nvidia_gpu`

<a id="get-api-system-gpu"></a>
### `GET /api/system/gpu`

Return raw GPU stats from nvidia-smi.

- Handler: [`get_gpu`](../../../backend/routers/system.py)
- Access: this computer only, or the API key once `ARYNWOOD_API_KEY` is set

**Response**

- `200`: JSON object with `available`, or JSON object with `available`, `name`, `temp`, `utilization`, `memory_used`, `memory_total`

<a id="get-api-system-gpu-queue"></a>
### `GET /api/system/gpu-queue`

Read-only view of the single-GPU serialization queue.

`gpu_queue` already tracks this to give callers queue-position visibility (see backend/services/gpu_jobs.py); this just exposes it so the UI's status drawer can say *why* a generate is sitting there rather than looking hung.

- Handler: [`get_gpu_queue`](../../../backend/routers/system.py)
- Access: this computer only, or the API key once `ARYNWOOD_API_KEY` is set

**Response**

- `200`: JSON object with `running`, `depth`, `waiting`

<a id="get-api-system-hardware"></a>
### `GET /api/system/hardware`

Returns hardware profile with capability hints for the UI.

- Handler: [`get_hardware`](../../../backend/routers/system.py)
- Access: this computer only, or the API key once `ARYNWOOD_API_KEY` is set

**Response**

- `200`: JSON object with `cpu` (JSON object with `name`, `cores`), `ram_gb`, `gpu` (JSON object with the fields of JSON object with `available`, or JSON object with `available`, `name`, `temp`, `utilization`, `memory_used`, `memory_total`, `vram_gb`), `disk_free_gb`, `can_run` (empty JSON list), `too_large` (empty JSON list), `ram_notes` (empty JSON list), `recommended_models` (JSON list, each item JSON object with `name`, `size`, `desc`, `pull`)

<a id="post-api-system-restart"></a>
### `POST /api/system/restart`

Restart the backend worker by touching backend/api.py.

uvicorn --reload only respawns the worker on file-change events — a SIGTERM to the worker leaves the reloader alive with no server behind it.

501 in a packaged build (see can_restart) rather than reporting "restarting" for something that will never happen.

- Handler: [`restart_backend`](../../../backend/routers/system.py)
- Access: this computer only, or the API key once `ARYNWOOD_API_KEY` is set

**Response**

- `200`: JSON object with `status`

**Errors** (plus the [access errors](../README.md#errors) every route can return)

| Status | Detail | Raised in |
|---|---|---|
| 501 | This build can't restart its own backend — quit and relaunch Arynwood. | `restart_backend` |

<a id="get-api-system-status"></a>
### `GET /api/system/status`

Parallel health check for Ollama, TTS, SD, Prometheus, and GPU.

- Handler: [`get_status`](../../../backend/routers/system.py)
- Access: this computer only, or the API key once `ARYNWOOD_API_KEY` is set

**Response**

- `200`: JSON object with `ollama`, `tortoise_tts`, `stable_diffusion`, `prometheus`, `gpu` (JSON object with `available`, or JSON object with `available`, `name`, `temp`, `utilization`, `memory_used`, `memory_total`), `platform`, `can_restart`, `cpu_mode` (JSON object with `enabled`, `setting`, `nvidia_gpu`)
